chapter: Haiti, Artie Shaw and Los Angeles work
title: The Gramercy Five with Artie Shaw: musicians and the McCarthy pressure
summary: Shaw's perfectionism and the quintet's quality; McCarthy-era pressure kept them from traveling, and afterwards Collins stayed with Billy Taylor's group.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: May I take you back to the Gramercy Five? (Inaudible).
Yes, you would. Like, that was a -- well, what can I say. Musically it was very interesting and worked quite a bit, and --

Well, Artie -- as you know Artie was a marvelous instrumentalist, you know, and he was a perfectionist also. So -- but he loved the group because we had a dynamite group, you know, with Billy and Charlie Smith, I think was one of the great drummers. He's dead now, he died quite young. But he was a great small band drummer, and a big band drummer. He could just -- he reminded me of Shadow Wilson in that respect, that he could play with a big band and really drive a big band or play with a small group and play brushes and whatever. But Charlie could -- immaculate taste. And of course what can I say. With Joe Benjamin there it was like the anchor, you know -- that was a color. You know, he colored the whole group. It was just a -- he painted a beautiful picture. So Artie was very happy with it, but as I said we couldn't keep the group, he couldn't keep the group because they were -- Joe McCarthy was closing in on us, you know, and it was very unfortunate.
You played with the Gramercy Five for two years?
Oh, no, I didn't play. We played together about -- oh, I guess about eight months, really. NO, no, I didn't play it.
Yeah, we recorded, and I really did quite a bit of work around Broadway and around New York. But

at that time he couldn't travel because you know, they were on him. And it was a very unfortunate thing as I said, because he liked the group and we loved working with him. But we worked together with -- well, after that Billy Taylor got his own little group and I worked with Billy for quite a bit, and Joe Benjamin and Charlie Smith and myself stayed -- you know, we stayed with Billy, yeah. And we worked quite a few clubs, and did quite a bit of recording with Billy. You know.
